- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤ -0.7) or shows strong negative momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and align with 3–5 day moving average.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is bullish; add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for first 3 days.
- Model overestimates in late horizon (25–30 days) when sentiment is bearish; reduce forecast by 1–2% for final 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing filter to forecast (e.g., 5-day moving average) to reduce volatility.
